title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in his notes on the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}, Grothendieck is building the combinatorics of the dual graphs of stable marked curves. He calls them '(m-)graphes', with 'bandes aplaties' (probably legs, i.e. marked points or half-edges going to infinity). The aim is to index the boundary strata of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification, and the maps between those strata, by graphs.

The previous page describes 'cutting' a graph G* along a set C of ordinary edges. One puts a point in the middle of each edge in C and cuts there. Each cut edge becomes two legs (marked points), which is the dual-graph shadow of partially normalizing the corresponding nodes. The result is a new graph with legs, possibly disconnected. One may then remove some legs and keep a union of connected components.

This page finishes that argument. Adding or removing legs does not change connected components ('kif-kif'). So cutting along C, then dropping some legs and some components, gives the most general relation between G and a G' of the kind allowed by his definition of 'morphismes de normalisation' of such graphs.

He then records formal properties:
(i) Normalization morphisms compose in the evident way.
(ii) A composite of strict normalization morphisms is strict.
(iii) Graphs with strict normalization morphisms form a category whose isomorphisms are the ordinary graph isomorphisms.
(iv) The morphisms of this category are monomorphisms (as read).
(v) As for 'générisation' morphisms (edge contractions, i.e. passing to a more generic stratum), the strict normalizations of G, taken up to unique isomorphism, form an ordered set. This ordered set is identified with the ordered set of subsets C of A(G), the edge set: a subset C gives the 'découpe' of G along C.

The next page uses this to get functors M_G(S) → M_{G'}(S) between moduli of G-'épinglées' special curves. These are the modular counterparts of the normalization (clutching) maps between boundary strata.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One point needs care: for the bijection 'strict normalizations of G ↔ subsets of A(G)' to hold up to unique isomorphism, the normalizations must be taken with their structure map to G (as objects over G). Graph automorphisms would otherwise spoil uniqueness. Grothendieck's 'à isomorphisme unique près' suggests he means exactly this.
The claim that all morphisms are monomorphisms is plausible for strict cuts (the edge and vertex data inject), but the reading of 'monomorphismes' is uncertain.

ideas.what: Normalization (cutting) morphisms of dual graphs: cut a set C of edges into pairs of legs, optionally forget legs and components. These correspond to partial normalization of nodes and to clutching maps between boundary strata.
ideas.modern_name: Cutting/grafting morphisms of stable graphs; clutching (gluing) morphisms ξ_Γ; structure maps of modular operads
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (1983) for clutching maps; Getzler–Kapranov (1998) and Behrend–Manin (1996) for the categorical graph formalism
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and the stratification at infinity informally, without this formalism

ideas.what: Composability of normalization morphisms; strict ones form a category whose isomorphisms are graph isomorphisms and whose morphisms are monomorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Category of stable graphs with cut morphisms

ideas.what: The ordered set of strict normalizations of G is identified with the ordered set of subsets of the edge set A(G), parallel to the analogous statement for generization (contraction) morphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Poset of partial normalizations / strata ≅ Boolean lattice of edge subsets (local structure of the boundary stratification)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of the dual-graph category governing the boundary of M̄_{g,n}. Cuts and contractions as two classes of graph morphisms are now standard (Knudsen clutching, Getzler–Kapranov, Chan–Galatius–Payne). It is of historical interest as an early, independent categorical treatment, but holds nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'ajouts[?] ou retraits[?]' reads as 'ajoutés ou retraits'. The following 'des bandes[?] [?]' is most likely 'des bandes aplaties'.
'm-graphes[?]': the graph name is uncertain throughout. It is perhaps 'MD-graphes' or a similar abbreviation, and the image is ambiguous.
Second paragraph: 'Les morphismes de cette catégorie sont des monomorphismes. Quand on se borne' reads as given. There is a struck-out word ('Quand' rewritten) before 'on se borne'.
'l'ens des sous-m-graphes[?] stricts' is more likely 'l'ens des normalisations (?) strictes d'un m-graphe G (à isomorphisme unique près) ... ordonné', i.e. an ordered set, not 'sous-graphes'.
Final line: 'the partie C(A(G))' should read approximately 'une partie C ⊂ A(G)' (or 'i.e. partie C de A(G)'), giving the bijection with subsets of the edge set.
Inserted above 'ordonné ... Ensuite': 'entre' / the struck word is likely 'isomorphes'. This matches the machine reading, but it is uncertain.
